events.title: EU sanctions against terrorism: Council lists the founder of 'The Base'
events.context: The Council expands its sanctions list to combat terrorism by designating the founder and leader of the EU-sanctioned organisation 'The Base'.

events.title: Budget de l'UE pour 2027: le Conseil donne son feu vert définitif
events.context: Le Conseil a donné son feu vert définitif sur le budget annuel de l'UE pour 2027, le septième et dernier budget annuel de l'actuel cadre financier pluriannuel (CFP) 2021-2027.

events.title: Sommet UE–Royaume-Uni à Bruxelles
events.context: L’Union européenne et le Royaume-Uni ont publié une déclaration commune à leur deuxième sommet. Ils ont réaffirmé leur engagement à appliquer l’accord de retrait.

events.title: Accord provisoire sur les importations d’énergies fossiles et le méthane
events.context: Le Conseil de l’UE et le Parlement européen ont annoncé un accord provisoire reportant de deux ans certaines obligations liées au méthane. Le report couvre des importations de gaz naturel, de pétrole brut et de charbon. L’adoption formelle constitue une étape distincte.

events.title: Durabilité: le Conseil et le Parlement parviennent à un accord sur la simplification des règles de transparence pour les produits financiers
events.context: Le Conseil et le Parlement européen sont parvenus à un accord provisoire sur la simplification des règles de transparence pour les produits financiers durables vendus dans l'UE.

events.title: Prime Minister Carney strengthens economic partnerships at APEC, capping an ambitious week that delivered major gains for Canadian workers and businesses
events.context: Canada is moving strategically, pragmatically, and decisively to secure greater access to new markets and attract new investment – building our strength at home and diversifying our partnerships abroad. To these ends, the Prime Minister, Mark Carney, represented Canada this week at the 33 rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting, in Shenzhen, China. There, APEC leaders outlined a shared vision for the Asia-Pacific to remain the world’s most dynamic and interconnected region. Prime Minister Carney emphasised the importance of predictable trade, resilient supply chains, and deeper economic integration in driving investment, innovation, and shared prosperity across the region. events.title: Prime Minister Carney advances Canada’s strategic partnership with China across trade, commerce, and culture
events.context: Over the past year and a half, Canada’s government has recalibrated our relationship with China – strategically, pragmatically, and decisively. Last January, the Prime Minister, Mark Carney, and the President of the People’s Republic of China, Xi Jinping, launched a new Canada-China strategic partnership to stabilise trade, build out clean energy industries, and better connect our peoples. Under the partnership, Canada and China have strengthened economic and financial cooperation, expanded cultural exchanges, and reduced tariffs on Canadian exports of canola seed and meal, peas, crab, and lobster. To date, Canada has restored market access for more than 90% of trade previously subject to tariff action – nearly $7.5 billion worth of Canadian exports.
